# Destroyed grids and editors never release their native ResizeObserver

## Context

`#17579` fixed `list.Buffered` by naming the component on **both** sides of the addon contract — `ResizeObserver[mounted ? 'register' : 'unregister']({componentId: id, id, windowId})` (`src/list/Buffered.mjs:167`). Its **Out of Scope** deferred exactly one thing: *"A repo-wide rewrite of other ResizeObserver consumers."* This is that follow-up, and the remaining consumers turn out to fail on the teardown side rather than the delivery side — which is why nothing surfaced when `#17579` closed.

The lane arrived from a different direction. `@neo-opus-vega` found `grid/Container.mjs#addResizeObserver` registering without `componentId` and asked whether it was a latent gap. It is not the same gap she fixed in `#17928`: grid's *delivery* works, because `DomEvent` registers grid's target correctly on its own path. Both of us then read the four sites as dead calls and converged on deleting them. That was wrong, and the disposition inverted on measurement: three of the four are cleanup that silently does nothing.

## The Problem

`src/main/addon/ResizeObserver.mjs#unregister` is **refcounted by `componentId`**, because one DOM target may be observed by several components:

```js
me.#targetToComponents[id] = componentIds.filter(cid => cid !== data.componentId);

if (me.#targetToComponents[id].length === 0) {
    delete me.#targetToComponents[id];
    me.#lastDispatchedSize.delete(id);
    node && me.instance.unobserve(node);
    me.syncPollState()
}
```

Every remaining consumer calls it as `unregister({id, windowId})`. `data.componentId` is `undefined`, so the filter removes only `undefined` entries and leaves every real one. The array never empties, so the guarded block never runs:

- `instance.unobserve(node)` never fires — the native observer keeps the detached node alive.
- `#lastDispatchedSize` keeps its entry.
- `syncPollState()` is never re-evaluated, so the hidden-document poll stays armed for a target nobody is watching.

For a live grid the array is `[gridId, undefined]`: `DomEvent.addResizeObserver` (`src/manager/DomEvent.mjs:131`) contributes the real id, and `grid/Container.mjs:343` contributes the `undefined`. Destroy strips the `undefined` and leaves `[gridId]` — length 1, not 0.

**Nothing else picks up the slack.** `DomEvent.unregister` (`src/manager/DomEvent.mjs:512`) is a `// todo` stub that `console.log`s and `return`s above its own body, and no unmount path calls the addon. These four call sites are the entire teardown surface for native ResizeObservers outside `list.Buffered`.

Consequence: every `grid.Container` and every `MonacoEditor` that is destroyed or unmounted leaves a native observer entry behind for the life of the document. Long-lived dashboards that create and drop grids accumulate them.

## The Architectural Reality

`componentId` is the **App-Worker delivery identity**; `id` is the **DOM target**. The addon keys observation by target and refcounts by component, which is what lets two components observe one node without either one's teardown blinding the other. A call that omits `componentId` is therefore not "the same call with less detail" — on register it adds an anonymous holder, and on unregister it asks to remove the anonymous holder specifically. `#17579` established this for delivery; the same asymmetry governs teardown.

Complete census of addon consumers (`grep -rn "addon.ResizeObserver\|getAddon('ResizeObserver')" src/ apps/`):

| site | call | `componentId` | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/manager/DomEvent.mjs:131` | register | ✅ | correct — the auto path for any `resize` domListener |
| `src/list/Buffered.mjs:167` | register + unregister | ✅ | correct — the `#17579` fix |
| `src/grid/Container.mjs:343` | register | ❌ | adds an anonymous holder |
| `src/grid/Container.mjs:346` | unregister (unmount) | ❌ | never releases |
| `src/grid/Container.mjs:1038` | unregister (destroy) | ❌ | never releases |
| `src/component/wrapper/MonacoEditor.mjs:386` | unregister (destroy) | ❌ | never releases |

`component/Canvas.mjs` and `container/Viewport.mjs` name the addon only in config JSDoc; both ride the `domListeners` path and are already covered by `DomEvent`.

## The Fix

Name the component on all four calls, matching `src/list/Buffered.mjs:167`:

1. `src/grid/Container.mjs#addResizeObserver` — `resizeParams` becomes `{componentId: me.id, id: me.id, windowId}`, covering both the register and unregister arms.
2. `src/grid/Container.mjs` destroy (`:1038`) — add `componentId: me.id`.
3. `src/component/wrapper/MonacoEditor.mjs` destroy (`:386`) — add `componentId: me.id`.

Both components' vdom roots carry no explicit id, so the DOM target is the component id and the addon's `includes` check collapses the manual register and `DomEvent`'s into one entry. Teardown then empties the array and reaches `unobserve`.

**Witness before fix.** `test/playwright/unit/main/addon/ResizeObserver.spec.mjs` already stands up the addon against a stubbed DOM. The arm drives a real component through mount and destroy and asserts the target is no longer observed — red on the current tree, green after. The addon itself is not modified: its refcount semantics are the correct contract, and asserting them directly would pass both before and after.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.main.addon.ResizeObserver#unregister` | `#17579`, unchanged here | removes the calling component from the target's holder list; unobserves when the list empties | a target with other holders stays observed, which is the point of the refcount | addon JSDoc | not modified by this ticket; the witness pins it from the caller side |
| `Neo.grid.Container#addResizeObserver` | this ticket | register and unregister both name `componentId: me.id` | an unmounted grid unregisters through the same params object | method JSDoc states why the id is named twice | destroy leaves zero observed targets |
| `Neo.component.wrapper.MonacoEditor#destroy` | this ticket | unregister names `componentId: me.id` | `me.mounted` guard unchanged | inline comment | destroy leaves zero observed targets |
| `Neo.manager.DomEvent#unregister` | `#17579` era, untouched | still a `// todo` stub | none | — | named here so the next reader does not assume teardown is centralized |

## Decision Record impact

`none`. This restores an existing contract established by `#17579`; it does not amend one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A unit arm drives a mounted component's destroy and asserts the native target is unobserved afterwards; it fails on the pre-fix tree.
- [ ] `src/grid/Container.mjs` names `componentId` on its register and unregister calls (`:343`, `:346`) and on destroy (`:1038`).
- [ ] `src/component/wrapper/MonacoEditor.mjs:386` names `componentId`.
- [ ] A census assertion or test comment records that `DomEvent.mjs:131` and `list/Buffered.mjs:167` are the two already-correct sites, so a later reader can tell coverage from omission.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit` green.

## Out of Scope

- **Implementing `DomEvent.unregister`.** The stub is named above so it is not mistaken for working teardown, but giving `DomEvent` a real unregister path is its own design question — it would centralize teardown and make the per-component calls redundant, which is a different ticket with a different blast radius.
- **The auto path's own teardown.** `DomEvent.addResizeObserver` registers and nothing ever unregisters that entry independently. Here the targets coincide with the components', so the fix drains them; a target registered only through a `delegate: '#other-id'` listener is not covered and is left as a known gap.
- **Removing the redundant register at `:343`.** With `DomEvent` already registering grid's target, grid's own register adds nothing once `componentId` is present — the addon dedups it. Deleting it is a simplification, not a correctness requirement, and keeping teardown self-contained is worth more than the line.
- **The dynamic-`addDomListeners` asymmetry.** Reading `updateDomListeners` says the auto path is deferred ~50ms on a mounted component rather than skipped. `@neo-opus-vega` then **measured** the opposite at the dock-maximize call site: reverting only the `componentId` on that register left `resizeEventCount: 0` across a 10s poll with real viewport resizes, so no auto registration reached that target at all. The gate that stops it there is unmeasured. Reading lost to measurement, and this ticket does not depend on the outcome — naming `componentId` on both of grid's own calls makes its holder self-contained, so teardown drains whether or not `DomEvent` also registered. `#17928` owns that seam; reproducer is the resize arm of `test/playwright/component/dashboard/DockMaximize.spec.mjs` plus the one-line revert.

## Avoided Traps

- **Deleting the four calls as dead code.** This was the working disposition until the refcount filter was read. A no-op teardown looks exactly like dead code from the call site and is the opposite: deleting it is the one edit that makes the leak permanent and unrecoverable by any later caller-side fix.
- **Arguing from symmetry with `#17928`.** Those sites do not share its premise — grid's delivery works. Symmetry would have produced the right edit for the wrong reason, and the wrong reason is what ends up in the next reader's head.
- **Fixing the addon instead of the callers.** `componentId`-keyed refcounting is deliberate; making `unregister` treat a missing `componentId` as "remove everything" would let one component blind another observing the same node.
